digests.summary_md: The restaurant batch captures a consumer skewing toward value and differentiated experiences, splitting chains that are building traffic from those still losing visits. LOCO, BJRI, and KRUS are converting menu innovation and guest frequency into comp gains and raised guidance, with BJRI’s traffic-only growth and active buybacks standing out. At the other extreme, ARKR feels the low-end pullback after holding prices flat, and PTLO is negotiating same-restaurant sales strain even as a new CEO pushes a national prototype rollout. The most radical story is BTBD’s planned exit from the industry via a merger into aerospace, a jarring pivot relative to the group. Incremental turnarounds populate the remainder: CBRL and RRGB are betting on guest-experience fixes, NDLS is pruning stores while targeting free cash flow, and STKS is converting weaker concepts into stronger brands. Capital-return activity surfaced through buybacks at CNNE, while a notable data gap leaves BDL, BH-A, GTIM, SG, and VSTD without relevant commentary today.
